auditor: independent Opus subagent (M5-2d precedent; RM18: assembly carried verbatim texts only, no judgment fields)

rows.why: Identical Flag-trait method sequence in the same order (is_switch/name_long/name_negated/doc_category/doc_short/doc_long/update); only literals ("no-messages"->"no-unicode", Category::Logging->Category::Search, doc text) and the LowArgs field name differ.
Token-for-token identical builder delegator `pub fn N(&mut self, yes: bool) -> &mut RegexMatcherBuilder { self.builder.N(yes); self }` with only the method name extended->jit renamed.

Same standard.rs printer-test template (max_columns(Some(46)), max_columns_preview(true), SHERLOCK.as_bytes(), assert_eq_printed!) but a inserts stats(true)+multi_line(true), which changes the pinned preview text from '[... omitted end of long line]' to '[... N more match(es)]'.

Identical delegator token sequence `pub fn N(&mut self, yes: bool) -> &mut B { self.F.N(yes); self }`; only the method name, the inner field (ig_builder vs builder) and the returned builder type are renamed across the two crates.

Both stamp the same switch-Flag skeleton ending in `args.FIELD = v.unwrap_switch(); Ok(())`; ByteOffset only adds a constant-returning name_short (Some(b'b')) accessor, exactly the kind of constant a parameterized stamp absorbs.

Both reuse the module's fixture harness verbatim (StandardBuilder::new()...build(NoColor::new(vec![])), search_reader(&matcher, SHERLOCK.as_bytes(), printer.sink(&matcher)), printer_contents, assert_eq_printed!) but the configured feature differs entirely: max_columns preview+stats vs only_matching+replacement with a different asserted output block.

Same Flag doc_* template, but PCRE2Version drops name_negated and its update asserts `v.unwrap_switch()` with a '--pcre2-version has no negation' message and sets args.special = Some(SpecialMode::VersionPCRE2) instead of assigning a bool field.

Shared Flag stamp with name_short/doc_* accessors, but FilesWithMatches has no name_negated and its update asserts then calls args.mode.update(Mode::Search(SearchMode::FilesWithMatches)), whereas FixedStrings does the plain bool assignment — no constant parameter covers both bodies.

The tmpdir fixture is copied verbatim (mkdirp 'a', the same five wfile calls for foo/a-foo/bar/a-bar, the same assert_paths(&["bar", "a", "a/bar"]) expectation), but one exercises add_custom_ignore_filename and the other add_ignore(&igpath) plus an extra is_none() assertion — a different builder entry point, not a value.

Bodies match down to the log::debug! format string 'ignoring {path}: found binary data at offset {binary_byte_offset}' and the quit_byte().is_some() guard; the only delta is `path.as_path().display()` vs `path.display()` forced by the differing path type, so either side could call one shared helper.

Both use the value-flag form (is_switch false, doc_variable Some(...)), but Regexp adds name_short(b'e') and its update runs convert::string then args.patterns.push(PatternSource::Regexp(..)), while FieldContextSeparator imports an alias and assigns Separator::new(&v.unwrap_value())? to one field.

Same SHERLOCK search_reader harness and assert_eq_printed! shape inherited from the module's test template, but b adds per_match/per_match_one_line/column configuration and pins column-prefixed 2-line output against a's plain 5-line line-numbered dump.

Both stamp the file's bench template `let x = new_*(CONST); b.iter(|| assert(x.matches(CONST)))` with paired constant families (SHORT_PAT/SHORT vs MANY_SHORT_GLOBS/MANY_SHORT_SEARCH), but the constructor and the assertion form (assert! vs assert_eq!(2, ...iter().count())) were adapted per benchmark.

Both repeat the file's flag-matrix block `let args = parse_low_raw([...]).unwrap(); assert_eq!(EnumVariant, args.FIELD)`, but the asserted enum type and field differ (CaseMode/args.case vs BinaryMode/args.binary) and b carries an extra precedence block, so no value parameter unifies them.

Statement-for-statement isomorphic: same tmpdir, same wfile('.gitignore')/wfile('.ignore') pair, same `let (ig, err) = IgnoreBuilder::new().build().add_child(td.path())` and is_whitelist() assertion; only the pattern literals change (a malformed '{foo' glob vs 'foo'), which flips err.is_some()/is_none() — all absorbable by a helper taking the two contents, the name and an expect-error bool.

Same delegator token sequence `pub fn N(&mut self, yes: bool) -> &mut B { self.F.N(yes); self }`; only the method name (require_git/jit_if_available), the inner field and the builder type identifier are renamed.

Bodies are token-identical — same `let mut count = 0`, loop over cls.iter() with the `count > self.limit_class` early return, `count += r.len()` and the final comparison; only the fn name and the hir::ClassBytes/hir::ClassUnicode parameter type identifier differ.

Identical switch-flag method set and doc_* skeleton, but LineBuffered's update branches `args.buffer = if v.unwrap_switch() { BufferMode::Line } else { BufferMode::Auto }` while OneFileSystem assigns the raw bool, so the update bodies differ in shape rather than in a constant.

Same Flag stamp including name_short, but InvertMatch is the switch form (is_switch true, name_negated Some("no-invert-match"), bool assign) and Replace is the value form (is_switch false, doc_variable Some("REPLACEMENT"), args.replace = Some(convert::string(v.unwrap_value())?.into())).

Same switch-flag skeleton and doc accessor order, but BlockBuffered's update selects BufferMode::Block/BufferMode::Auto through an if/else while NoMessages writes v.unwrap_switch() straight into a bool field — an adaptation a constant parameter cannot carry.

Identical three-block negation test (parse_low_raw(None::<&str>), the flag, then flag + no-flag) with assert_eq!(false/true/false, args.FIELD); only the flag-name string literals and the field identifier are renamed, the rest is line wrapping.

Both are the same `fn update(&self, v: FlagValue, args: &mut LowArgs) -> anyhow::Result<()>` with body `args.FIELD = v.unwrap_switch(); Ok(())`; the only token that differs is no_ignore_messages vs no_ignore_parent.

Same doc_category/doc_short/doc_long template, but the flag kind was changed: BlockBuffered is a switch (is_switch true, name_negated, BufferMode if/else) while RegexSizeLimit is a value flag (is_switch false, doc_variable Some("NUM+SUFFIX?"), convert::human_readable_usize on v.unwrap_value()).
